research_question: Does coupling scheduled trusted full-goal observation with immediate invocation of the existing atomic submit-and-replay action preserve a usable candidate and return target-state counterexamples early enough for the same Agent session to repair them?

selection.source: Consumed development trajectories from the screened Bad-6 study and the atomic rescue diagnostic
selection.rule: Select the three observed goal-to-delivery cases: quacc and hark passed the full goal well before voluntary atomic submission, while ajenti repeatedly passed the full goal but never submitted. Exclude micropy-cli because its current atomic diagnostic never reached the full goal, so this treatment could not activate.
selection.outcome_conditioning: Intentional mechanism qualification on consumed cases; this is not an unbiased effectiveness or generalization sample.

treatment.description: Keep the Agent's shell search unrestricted. After a scheduled trusted full-goal observation passes, force the next model action to use the same submit_bootstrap action exposed by the atomic control. A replay failure returns raw executable feedback and restores free tool choice in the same session.

shared_with_atomic_control: visible tools and submit_bootstrap action signature
minimal evaluator and repository integrity boundary
treatment_differences: The harness periodically executes the trusted full goal after shell operations and returns that observation to the Agent.
When that observation reports candidate_ready=true, the next model request is constrained to the already available submit_bootstrap action instead of waiting for voluntary submission.
comparability.attribution_limit: This consumed pilot qualifies the coupled scheduled-observation plus atomic-handoff mechanism. It does not estimate a pure handoff effect independently of scheduled observation.
comparability.historical_comparator: The in-progress atomic rescue runs are descriptive comparators only because independent model rollouts are stochastic.

measurements.endpoint: EnvBench Official Pass for each scheduled episode

interpretation: A prompt observation-triggered handoff with earlier replay feedback supports the proposed goal-to-delivery mechanism.
Official rescue on these cases is development evidence, not a population effect estimate.
Failure to reach the full goal is outside this treatment's mechanism and must not be relabeled as a handoff failure.
Transient provider or package-network failures are reported separately from dependency-semantic and delivery failures.
restrictions: Do not add case-specific package mappings, commands, checkpoints, or operation restrictions.
Do not change the trusted goal, integrity boundary, or replay implementation between the atomic comparator and treatment.
Do not use these consumed outcomes as held-out, leaderboard, statistical-significance, or SOTA evidence.
